breaking.change: The loading screen is redrawn in the HUD's language over its key art: an eyebrow (Now entering) over the place in large condensed bold, the tip on a cut smoked-glass plate with a Tip tag and a Next tip button (Tab on a key cap; a 44 px target on a touch screen), and the progress as the HUD's leaning bar with a white lead edge, a spinner while it is not ready and the figure, which turns to the accent once ready. Continue is a lit bevelled button (Enter on a key cap; Tap to continue on a touch screen). The tip is no longer clamped to four lines, and a shade rises behind the words and grows with them, so a long place name stays readable over bright art. Without key art the style's placeholder is a dark wash lit by the accent instead of a picture glyph. The `<progress>` control is replaced by the bar: the screen now uses the Spinner component and no longer uses control:progress. New prop status (what the wait is for, beside the figure). New parts loading.eyebrow, .label, .next, .bar, .fill, .figure and .status; loading.scrim, .frame and .title stay, and .frame is the tip plate (no longer a panel). New string keys screen.loading.busy, .continueKey, .entering, .next, .nextKey and .tapContinue.
breaking.fix: A style that dressed the loading screen's `progress` element dresses loading.bar and loading.fill (or sets the --loading-fill, --bar-well and --bar-rim tokens). A style that gave loading.frame a panel's look sets the --hud-plate-* tokens instead. A game that translates the screen adds the six new string keys to its tables.

fixed.summary: On a phone at 150 % text a long tip was cut with an ellipsis after four lines; it now wraps whole.
